subject: Post-call: FinTechCo competitive & multi-region perf follow-ups
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: FinTechCo competitive & multi-region perf follow-ups

Thanks for the call this morning - good discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call summary
- Use case: customer-facing recommendations and real-time personalization across US and EU.
- Primary objectives: consistent p95 latency under 120ms, data residency in EU for EU traffic, and predictable unit costs compared to hyperscaler inference APIs.
- Concerns raised: regional availability, egress costs, and ability to run private VPC endpoints for sensitive flows.

Redwood differentiators vs hyperscalers (short)
- Unified runtime with explicit routing policies so you can target EU-only nodes for EU users without managing separate endpoints.
- Cost controls: batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost vs single-request hyperscaler endpoints.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted API now, Dedicated pools or Private VPC for strict residency and audit needs.
- SLA and fallbacks: multi-region routing with automatic fallback to compatible model variant if a region is degraded.

Proposed next tests (what we can do this week)
1) Synthetic latency pings: run simple HTTP ping and full 1-token generation from US-East, EU-West, and APAC egress to capture cold and warm p95. We can provide curl examples and a small script.
2) Egress cost comparison: we will provide per-token cost estimates including typical batching scenarios and an example workload.
3) Data residency test: demo routing for EU-only traffic and sample audit logs to show residency controls.
4) If you want, a short Dedicated/Private preview to validate VPC peering and KMS integration.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscalers-comparison.pdf (high-level), SOC2-answers.docx (security questions).

Next steps and asks for FinTechCo
- Can you share a network contact or allow netops to run synthetic pings? preferred windows: 2026-03-11 or 2026-03-12.
- Are there any specific residency or compliance constraints beyond EU-only at rest and in-region processing?

I will loop in Marissa to propose exact test steps and provide the pings script. Happy to jump on a 30 minute test coordination call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
---
Redwood Inference

- Can you confirm which regions you currently have public endpoints in and which ones support EU-only routing today? We need concrete region names (eg eu-west-1).
- For the egress cost calc, do you have a sample calculation for a 1000 qps steady-state workload with 2 token responses on average? That will help our finance team compare to our current hyperscaler bill.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@fintechco.com>, Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@fintechco.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-11T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Post-call: FinTechCo competitive & multi-region perf follow-ups - test plan

Hi Alex, Priya - thanks for the quick reply. Below is a concise technical plan for the synthetic tests and what we can provide.

Test plan (short)
1) Latency pings (connectivity): from three vantage points - US-East (ashburn), EU-West (dublin), APAC (singapore). We will ask your netops to run both TCP latency and full TLS handshake + one-token API call. Expected outputs: RTT, TLS handshake time, p50/p95/p99 for 1-token generation warm/cold.
2) Full generation test: 1-token and 16-token scenarios with and without batching to show batching efficiency.
3) Data residency routing check: we will demonstrate routing a request with header X-Region: eu to EU-only nodes and provide audit log entries showing node location and KMS key id prefix.

Commands we suggest for netops (example)
- curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Region: eu' -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' -w '\nSTATUS:%{http_code} TOTAL_TIME:%{time_total}\n'

We ran a quick internal smoke test yesterday and attached the raw CSV: latency-report-us-eu-20260311.csv - it includes warm and cold p95 across EU/US vantage points. Early takeaways: EU warm p95 for single token generation is 78ms from Dublin to our EU nodes; US warm p95 is 65ms from Ashburn to our US nodes. We can run identical tests from your netops to compare.

Attachments: latency-report-us-eu-20260311.csv (raw), small script to run pings.

Let me know a time for a short coordination call or we can run asynchronously - whichever you prefer.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Alex and team - appreciate the deep questions. Quick commercial context while we run the tests: 
- Trial credits: we can offer a 30 day eval credit covering test traffic and a small PoC for dedicated routing. I will have our finance team scope this once Jordan and Laura confirm expected test volume.
- Pricing: we will send a modeled comparison for 1000 qps and 2 token avg later today. Note that our modeled per-token cost with batching assumptions typically drives 20-35% unit cost savings vs equivalent on-demand hyperscaler endpoints for similar throughput.
- Procurement: if you need a short evaluation agreement or NDA, we can push via DocuSign. Link included.

Laura - can you own onboarding and the eval agreement? Jordan - please coordinate the credit sizing with Alex.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
